Block engines

Source: R/engines.R
indri_engine.Rd

The per-subset fit is a plugin. An engine is a list with a name, a capabilities list and a fit function with the signature fit(Y, X, a_forms, control) returning at least G and E (on the standardised scale, in the column order of Y), plus either posterior draws (an s by s by D array; stanimal) or se and vcov, the joint sampling covariance of the lower-triangle G entries (the REML engines), from which fit_G() draws.

Usage

indri_engine(name = "stanimal")

indri_engines()

Arguments

name

Engine name.

Value

An engine list.

indri_engines() returns the names of the implemented engines.

Details

LiMMBo delegates its subset fits to limix; indri delegates to stanimal, sommer, ASReml-R or the WOMBAT program, because the right engine depends on the number of individuals, on whether the data have gaps, on whether a licence is available, and on whether the caller wants a posterior or a likelihood. WOMBAT is a standalone REML program (Linux and Windows, free for academic use); the "wombat" engine finds it through engine_args = list(wombat = <path>), options(indri.wombat = <path>) or the PATH, engine_args = list(wombat_dir = <dir>) keeps a block's WOMBAT files for inspection, and engine_args = list(wombat_rank = q) fits G at reduced rank q (the residual stays full rank).

Examples

# Inspect the registry without fitting a model or loading an engine.
indri_engines()
#> [1] "stanimal" "sommer"   "asreml"   "wombat"  
engine <- indri_engine("sommer")
engine$name
#> [1] "sommer"
engine$capabilities
#> $draws
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $se
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $vcov
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $a_form
#> [1] "inverse"
#> 
#> $missing
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $default_s
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $default_cooccurrence
#> [1] 1
#>
